A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original representation analyses, attention-knockout experiments, activation patching, and masked fine-tuning results in Sections 3–4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains these original empirical analyses and experimental results, including the supplementary model comparisons and ablations.

M1.justification: The representation analyses, attention knockout, activation patching, Emu3 adaptation, and masked [EOI] fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged in Sections 2–4 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet animal tasks, VQAv2 questions, Flickr30k and MS-COCO captioning data, and LLaVA-instruct training data. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The Chameleon, Emu3, LLaVA, Pixtral, Janus, and VILA-U comparisons retain the same membership within corresponding experiments. The ablation and fine-tuning controls are unchanged; the newly cited studies are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 2–4 and Appendix B retain the same sampling, prompts, model configurations, metrics, and training settings, including the 2,000-example ablation evaluations. Changes such as '20 class' to '20 classes' are grammatical.

E4.justification: The token knockouts, semantic-localization analyses across models and tasks, activation-patching experiments, and fine-tuning robustness comparisons are retained. Appendix C adds no new analysis or ablation.

E5.justification: Figures 2 and A1 retain median and interquartile-range reporting, and Appendix B.4 retains its clustering t-test description. Repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, and significance-reporting practices do not change.

E6.justification: The numerical table entries and plotted results are unchanged. For example, both versions report Chameleon-7B VQAv2 scores of 0.51 without ablation and 0.25 with [EOI] attention removed in Tables 1 and A3.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), defining cross-modal attention, neighborhood overlap, and output-distribution similarity, are unchanged. Appendix B.4 also retains the same clustering mathematics; no formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about modality separation, localized [EOI] communication in native models, distributed communication in non-native models, and intervention through patching and fine-tuning.

C2.justification: The causal interpretation of [EOI], the proposed architectural and training explanations, and the stated limitations remain substantively unchanged. Section 5 still limits applicability by communication direction, architecture coverage, and modality coverage.

D1.justification: The model-access references, hardware disclosure, code URL, prompts, and fine-tuning hyperparameters are retained. The code URL merely wraps differently, and updated organizational names in references do not change access information.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds Basile et al., Head Pursuit, and Ortu et al., When Seeing Overrides Knowing, as v4 references 60–61. Its discussion now acknowledges visual information localized in deeper attention heads alongside spatially localized image tokens.

P1.justification: There are scattered grammar and punctuation corrections, paragraph merges, bibliographic metadata updates, and a revised Appendix A paragraph retitled 'Localization of information in Text-Only VLMs.' The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Text placement, spacing around figures and tables, and page breaks reflow; Section 5 begins on PDF page 10 instead of page 9. The figure and table sets, plotted graphics, axes, legends, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised Appendix A provides a more complete account of prior work by recognizing localization in deeper attention heads, while small copyedits improve readability. These are limited improvements in context and presentation; the methods, empirical support, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
